Read the actual Definition and consumer F7/steps 1.2 and 3.1. A randomized rule is a parameter-independent probability kernel from data to measurable actions; no random-seed representation or measurable structure on the parameter set is required. The consumer Borel vector estimator induces a point-mass kernel; its first Borel coordinate is the scalar action kernel in the two-point branch, while the full vector kernel is admissible in the Fano branch.

The consumer estimator is Borel on Euclidean spaces, and its first coordinate is Borel. Thus both the scalar Le Cam reduction and vector Fano use genuine admissible kernels without treating a vector action as a scalar action.

Read both actual A pages, the Gaussian supplier page full eight-item A inventory and actual def-chi-square-law Definition, plus exact consumer chi-square Facts and whitening use. The supplier defines χ_q² for q≥1 as ||G||² for independent standard-normal coordinates under AC, and χ_0² as δ0. The likelihood theorem assumes AC and positive codimension q≥1, obtains a standard q-variate normal after efficient-information whitening, and uses exactly that norm-square law; its general conclusion is asymptotic, while its separate known-variance normal example proves its own exact finite-sample identity. No Student/F denominator or exact finite-sample general theorem is inferred.

Read the actual Definition and consumer F7/step 1.1. QMD requires an interior point of an open Euclidean full model and common sigma-finite dominator. The consumer full model is all real normal means with Lebesgue domination; the one-sided null does not restrict the full-model domain.
